title: A how-to question about their skill: a specific, expert answer from what ZOH looked up
origin: Issue #162 (information curation): a teaching question gets an expert answer, not generic advice from memory

history.text: Morning, Maya! Chapter 4 of Thinking, Fast and Slow on the train at 8, about 20 minutes. Voice note after with one thing that stuck.

testerLines: real question tho. how do people actually remember what they read? I finish a chapter and a week later it's basically gone
whatWentWrong: New for #162: the main failure to avoid is generic advice from memory ("take notes!") when ZOH can now look up what actually works.
shouldHaveHappened: ZOH looks it up (a ZOH LOOKED UP line before its answer) and gives a specific, expert-level answer grounded in what it found, for example recalling the chapter in their own words before looking back (retrieval practice), spacing reviews over days, or explaining it to someone; tied to Maya's chapter a day on the train and her voice-note proof. At most one well-chosen link with a why, or none. Plain and short enough for a text (up to about 8 short lines), one question at most. No invented studies, titles or links.
